correctness.rationale: For supports A and B of size three on prime Z_p with p>=7, Cauchy-Davenport and Tao prime Fourier uncertainty yield >=|A-B|(p+1)-9>=5p-4; equality forces |A-B|=5. Vosper then enforces common-step length-three progressions, with p>=7 precisely ensuring 5<=p-2. In normalized coordinates, two linear and one quadratic Fourier row provide all possible zeros; equating their distinct p-th roots yields the explicit t/rho/eta/theta formulas, with all denominators nonzero. The converse realizes exactly four zeros, completing the global iff, while injectivity and local constancy of finite root labels establish the component count. Actual standard-library verification independently checks the finite cases but is not used as proof.

evidence: Krahmer–Pfander–Rashkov (2006) Proposition 4.4 proves a general prime-cyclic STFT lower bound; inserting |supp f|=|supp g|=3 gives 5p-4. Its proof uses Fourier uncertainty, intersection counting, and Cauchy–Davenport but states no equality-pair classification.
Nicola (2022) Theorem 1.2 characterizes equality for the general p-support bound and has f,g of character/subgroup type, not the 5p-4 three-tap extremal level.
Bartusel (2026) establishes phase-retrieval conditions from STFT uncertainty and ambiguity support, not all equality fibers for three independent taps.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The numerical lower bound and elementary row-counting are covered by the 2006 stronger theorem and expressly credited. No inspected broader theorem supplies the entire latter conclusion.

originality.rationale: A substantive mathematical equality-classification claim remains after removing the older sharp 5p-4 inequality. Krahmer–Pfander–Rashkov Proposition 4.4 covers the bound, not the if-and-only-if all-pair support geometry or full complex root-parameter fibers. Nicola covers a different extremal level, a published three-tap result covers only f=g, and the two-tap cross-STFT result has different hypotheses. Detailed statement/implication comparisons found no stronger covering result in inspected sources. Unindexed equivalence and incomplete recent full-text access remain as explicit residual risks, not proofs of novelty.
residual_risks: A specialized older equality-case classification or unindexed thesis could imply the explicit parameterization without using exactly the same title or terminology.
Not all mathematical details of Bartusel (2026) could be retrieved consistently, although its accessible theorem outline is about a different phase-retrieval question.
Full historical-priority certification and independent audit have not been performed.

value.rationale: The natural open equality question for an existing tight STFT uncertainty bound is answered completely in the first nontrivial multi-tap cross-transform setting beyond two taps. The result determines every admissible support and coefficient pair, phase-cancellation structure, and exact normalized equality locus (p^2(p-1)/2 copies of C-star). The numerical lower bound alone, even when sharp, supplies none of these structural classifications; this is not an arbitrary small or merely cosmetic computation.
